summary: The article describes the growing trend of outdoor yoga and fitness classes in city parks, including 'Fitness Flash Mobs'. It profiles instructors and their named classes, from sunrise bootcamps to moonlit yoga, family and inclusive sessions, and office-break workouts. It concludes that these classes are a lifestyle change and community builder that is gaining momentum.
one_line: Outdoor yoga and fitness classes in city parks are booming, with instructors launching sunrise, moonlit, family, inclusive and office-break sessions.
key_facts: Emily Parker of 'Breathe & Stretch' introduced 'Sunrise Salutations' on September 3, 2023 and has seen a steady rise in attendance.
Anthony Jacobs, a certified fitness trainer, launched the high-intensity 'Pump in the Park' on September 15.
Local yoga influencer Lila Nguyen hosted a 'Fitness Flash Mob' on September 20 that went viral.
Marcus Reed's bootcamp 'Reed Routines' started October 1, with lunges, sprints and core exercises finished before the city stirs.
Yoga teacher Samantha Woods introduced 'Lunar Flow' on September 25, practiced under the moon and LED lights.
Thomas Keller, a renowned athlete, opened functional fitness trails on September 30, using benches for box jumps and monkey bars for pull-ups.
Ellie Tan hosted 'Autumn Abs' on November 1, with attendees encouraged to dress in layers.
Julie Henderson, a mother and fitness coach, started the weekend class 'Family Fundamentals' last September, with tag games and partner yoga poses.
Certified instructor John Ellis has led the 'Everyone Can Yoga' series every Sunday since September 18, focusing on modifications for all abilities.
Corporate wellness coach Rachel Simmons created 'Desk Detox Sessions', in demand since October 5, combining short exercise bursts with mindfulness.
Social media hashtags like #ParkWorkout and #YogaWithAView drive interest in park classes.
Henderson Park is mentioned as a place where communities cheer each other on through burpees and squats.
